 Pulaski County election run-offs set for Dec. 1
 1 hour, 20 minutes ago 
 by 
 Grant Lancaster 
 -->
 -->
 -->
 -->
 Comments 
 Commissioner Marianne Harrington looks over spreadsheets of provisional ballots during the Pulaski County Board of Election Commissioners meeting Monday, Nov. 9, 2026 in Little Rock. (Arkansas Democrat-Gazette/Staci Vandagriff) 
 Let us read it for you. Listen now. 
 Your browser does not support the audio element.
 Mayoral races in Sherwood and Jacksonville and two city council contests are set for runoff elections in Pulaski County, according to an public notice for voters the Pulaski County Election Commission approved Monday.
 The commission set the runoff election for Dec. 1, with early voting from Nov. 24-30, election coordinator Amanda Dickens said.
 In Sherwood, the contest between Mayor Mary Jo Heye-Townsell and Mike Willingham is so close that the provisional ballots the commissioners approved Monday afternoon may eliminate the need for a runoff, Dickens said. Heye-Townsell currently holds the majority by just eight votes, Dickens said.
 Dickens estimated the commissioners approved about 270 of the more than 800 provisional ballots up for review on Monday, but didn't provide an estimate for the number they rejected or agreed to reconsider in their Friday meeting, during which they are set to certify the election results. The notice to voters could be modified if a runoff in Sherwood isn't necessary, Dickens said.
 Jacksonville Mayor Jeff Elmore won fewer votes than challenger James Bolden III, according to preliminary results, but Bolden is short of winning a majority.
 The runoff election for North Little Rock council member for Ward 2 Position 2 would pit Marvin Benton against Anna Beth Gorman, the notice states. Benton led on election night with 1,672 votes, according to preliminary results, but fell short of winning the majority of votes in the four-way contest.
 Preliminary results for the Alexander city council's Ward 4 Position 2 show incumbent Juanita Wilson in the lead with 18 of the 34 total votes count. The notice lists challenger Trevis Bentley, who won 10 votes according to preliminary results, as Wilson's competitor in the runoff.
 All of the races set for runoff are nonpartisan positions.
 Early voting for the runoff elections will be on weekdays only, excluding Thanksgiving Day, and the notice will include details about polling locations. Dickens listed the Pulaski County Election Commission building on West Markham Street in Little Rock as an early voting location as well as North Little Rock's Laman Library, the Jacksonville Community Center and First Christian Church in Sherwood.
 Dickens has not received any requests for recounts in the Pulaski County midterm elections, she told the commissioners.
 Heye-Townsell, who took office in 2023 after serving on the Sherwood city council, faced challenges from Willingham, Jay Bir and Nara Smith. Willingham is the chief operating officer of the healthcare organization RegenaDerm, Smith is a teacher and financial adviser and Bir is an analyst for the Arkansas Department of Shared Administrative Services.
 Elmore has been Jacksonville mayor since 2023. Bolden is a retired Air Force first sergeant and a pastor at Evangelistic Ministries Church and Kevin Cole, who came in third in last week's election, is a retired Army National Guard staff sergeant who worked as an engineer in the Jacksonville Street Department for 20 years.
 Grant Lancaster 
 glancaster@adgnewsroom.com 
 Grant Lancaster covers crime, policing and breaking news for the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette. A Little Rock native, his articles focus primarily on crime and law enforcement efforts in Pulaski County, although he reports on other parts of the state as well.
